hints.title: Ranking Without Numeric Gaps
hints.text: Standard competition ranking skips subsequent numbers when ties occur. How can each distinct numerical score receive consecutive rank integers ordered from highest to lowest without leaving any gaps?

hints.title: Dense Window Ranking Invariant
hints.text: A dense ranking function assigns identical ranking positions to tied values while incrementing by exactly one for the next distinct score in the partition.

hints.title: Dense Rank Window Specification
hints.text: Apply the dense ranking window function ordered by score in descending order over the entire table. Assign the column alias rank with identifier delimiters if required by the dialect.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
SELECT score, DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY score DESC) AS `rank`
FROM Scores;
```

variables: N: total score rows in Scores table
complexity.notes: Single pass window sort and dense rank assignment across score values.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Correlated subqueries counting distinct higher scores per row take O(N^2) time, choking on large score tables.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Window ranking sorts records in O(N log N) time and evaluates rank increments in a single pass using O(N) memory.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Using DENSE_RANK() instead of RANK() or ROW_NUMBER(), properly aliasing rank using backticks or identifier quotes.

solutions.code:
SELECT score, DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY score DESC) AS `rank`
FROM Scores;

SELECT score, DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY score DESC) AS "rank"
FROM Scores;

solutions.approach: Pandas Dense Rank by Score Descending
